recipes.name: Pork Stroganoff
ingredients_raw: 2 tablespoons chopped fresh parsley, for garnish

steps.text: Heat oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Cook chops in hot oil until well browned on both sides. Remove chops to a plate; set aside.

Add onion and mushrooms to drippings in the skillet and cook until tender, stirring occasionally. Mix in water, mustard, and salt. Return chops to the skillet and bring to a boil. Reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 1 hour.
Remove chops to a warm platter. Whisk sour cream into sauce in the skillet; heat through, but do not boil. Pour over chops and garnish with parsley to serve.

raw_recipe.headline: Pork Stroganoff
raw_recipe.description: This pork stroganoff is easy-to-make comfort food featuring thick-cut chops, onions, and mushrooms served with a rich, enticing sour cream sauce.

review.reviewBody:
It was absolutely amazing!
I didn't think it would be THAT good...but it turned out to be super duper tasty.
My wife and I devoured it all and couldn't stop talking about how good it was.
This is definetely not the last time I make this one. Awesome.
I've made this dish many times now and I've learned that the cooking time of 1 hour is a bit much.
I usually cook it about 30 minutes and it's fine.
I sometimes do the hour but only on VERY low heat or else it gets too dry. 
Plus I put 2 cups of Sour cream instead of 1/2 a cup.
It just seems better that way. 1/2 a cup just didn't cut it.
Also lately I've been cutting the pork into cubes and mixing it all up and then pouring it over egg noodles. I like it better that way instead of the big pork chops. Both ways are good though

This recipe is very good I do however could not resist to add paprika, a tsp of tomato paste and a tsp of lemon. Without the tangyness of the lemon and the smoky flavor of paprika, I would feel that my stroganoff would be lacking something very important! If you want a bit of extra thickness add a tbsp of flour.

used leftover pork tenderloin that I had roasted coated with Dijon mustard and Italian herbs so didn't add any additional mustard. I doubled the amount of mushrooms, liquid and sour cream, and used chicken stock instead of water. Also added a chopped scallion to the sautéed veggies. Served over buttered and peppered egg noodles. Fantastic.

I cubed up a pound of parchment roasted pork loin along with jelly, doubled the sour cream with a pinch of powdered lemon peel, and l added a good bit of ground black pepper to the onions at the start. I cooked the onions until translucent before adding the mushrooms. I also added a cup of beef broth at the simmering stage. So delicious!

Added extra onions, used the pork drippings instead of water, used a pork shoulder as the leftover pork, fresh garlic, placed over wide noodles but white rice would work too even bow ties The pork was already cooked so the cooking time simmer, easily changed with tenderness. Fresh parsley and chives as garnish. Good stuff in, good food out. Very easy. I used the recipe as a boiler plate but improvised. Still lots of room for mistakes. Keep in mind not to over season with salt as the pork may have been salted prior. Oh Dijon mustard instead of prepared much better!!!!!

I made this recipe with Mojo marinated pork that was leftover from making Cuban sandwiches. So the pork was already cooked. I did the recipe as directed, except I simmered it for just 20 minutes. Then I mixed it with a prepared bag of egg noodles. Fantastic flavor!

My husband is not one to ooooh and aaaah over food, but he really did on this one. He loved how "light" it tasted. (Not like it cream of mushroom soup from the can. hahaha) 
Go for it. Try it. You'll be pleasantly surprised. 
This time I used pork loin cut in thick strips and it was easier than chops. I go very easy on the mustard and heavy on sour cream. lol And like others, I didn't cook it as long, perhaps 40 minutes. I also watch the water and add more if needed. Oh, and I added lots of garlic this last time.
Excellent recipe! I cut the pork into chunks and cooked them in my air fryer. I cooked the mushrooms (8 oz) and onions on the stovetop, then added the pork, mustard and sour cream. Delicious!

I seriously don’t know why everyone didn’t give this 5 stars. I followed the recipe pretty closely but used boneless country style pork ribs, which are already tender. Also when I sautéd the pork, I used a stainless steel pot. The fond develops very well, so there’s more flavor to scrape up when you put the onions and mushrooms in. I put the finished pork stroganoff over rice, as my husband prefers. He gave the highest compliment for him; “It’s pretty good.” 😊

Used cubed pork tenderloin and replaced water with white wine and increased the amount of ingredients in sauce according to the amount of pork tenderloin I used. Since I used cubed pork tenderloin, I reduced cooking time once the pork was back in sauce to a few minutes, until pork was done and the sauce was heated through. Served over noodles. Finished with dill.

I used leftover pork roast which I cut in strips and sautéed in butter along with the mushrooms. That helped bring out the pork drippings and flavor. IMHO this recipe needs four or five times as much water (better yet, broth) and a splash or two of Worcestershire sauce. I added about a tablespoon of corn starch (mixed with small amount of broth) to thicken the gravy. Great over noodles.

I really liked this, and I will definitely it make again. I did salt and pepper the pork chops before searing them (I kind of thought that was a given), and I always add a little salt when I sauté onions (again a given for how I cook). The only variation is that I added some paprika with the mustard as one reviewer recommended, I read the review and thought the color would be nice. Otherwise I stuck with the recipe, and was really pleased with how it came out, and I like that it’s easy to tweak to your preferences. I’m looking forward to adding sage as another reviewer recommended as I like sage. That said the amount of mustard seemed spot on (I don’t cook with mustard much), and really made for a nice sauce. I’m not a huge fan of pork, but it’s been on sale lately, so it’s nice to have another way to use it. I agree with another reviewer that if you use left over pork the sauce will be lacking, which is not to say I would not do this, but I would not do this, and then leave a negative review: pan drippings are obviously a large component of the sauce. I also like that it can be paired with really any starch you have on hand. We had it with noodles, but next time I’ll likely serve it with mashed potatoes. I also like how the simmer time provides time to make a side vegetable, and if you are doing the low carb things it would be lovely atop steamed or roasted vegetables. Thank you recipe poster! My family and I really enjoyed this!!
Great. I added about 2 cups sour cream and forgot the mustard. Used leftover pork roast. Everyone loved it!

Good recipe. People who make it from leftover precooked pork dont realize they are kind of changing the recipe and not getting the drippings/flavors you'd normally get from cooking the pork form fresh.

I just made this for dinner using a left over bacon wrapped pork loin. It was really good! I doubled the water & sour cream and added a lipton beef and onion packet for flavors. Added cooked egg noodles at the end. SO good 👍👍
I brown the cut-up pork chops in the skillet with the sauteed onions and mushrooms, and then add the rest of the ingredients.
I substituted the chops for loin, cooked slowly, and added a few more spices, a very big hit at any dinner function.

I made this for dinner tonight. I used pork loin and vegetable stock from the water. I also salted and peppered the pork, otherwise made it per recipe. In the end, it needed something and I added a tablespoon of lemon juice. WOW it was delicious, I will make this again. I did serve it with steamed broccoli, instead of noodles... yummy...

This was a hit in our house. Like a few others, I decided to add more flavor by using beef broth instead of water as the liquid. I used one can of broth and added water as it simmered down in order to have enough sauce. I also thickened it with a little corn starch at the end and cut up the pork as well.

Quick and easy for a weeknight meal. I doubled the sour cream, but I still felt it lacked that sour cream bite I like. I doubled the mushrooms as I do with most recipes since I do like mushrooms. I cooked 2 cups of egg noodles which turned out to be just right.
